findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the silicone sealant (caulking) to be damaged or inadequate around the hot line units and counter to the left of the dish machine. Ensure these areas are repaired prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: The inspector observed a small freshwater leak at the mop sink as well as a leak at the dish area hand sink. The PIC was informed and maintenance will be scheduled for the plumbing concerns. Ensure these repairs are completed prior to the next routine inspection (at least 90 days).
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed employee fail to use a barrier to turn off the hand sink after washing hands. PIC was informed that a barrier such as a paper towel should be used to turn off the hand sink to prevent cross-contamination. Ensure all staff members are properly hand washing at all times.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an employee fail to wash their hands before donning new gloves to portion food for the dessert bar. The PIC was informed and education was conducted regarding proper handwashing. Ensure staff are washing their hands before putting on new gloves to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Inspector observed knives and a pair of scissors stored inside of counters or equipment which is not considered easily cleanable. Ensure utensils are stored in designated areas to avoid contamination. The PIC was informed and the utensils were sent to the dish area.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.12(A)(1) and A(3)-(8) Prohibitions. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, cleaned and SANITIZED EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES may not be stored: (1) In locker rooms; (3) In garbage rooms; (4) In mechanical rooms; (5) Under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips; (6) Under leaking water lines including leaking automatic fire sprinkler heads or under lines on which water has condensed; (7) Under open stairwells; or (8) Under other sources of contamination.

findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

Observed handle of ice scoop touching the ice at the small wait station. Scoop was removed with tongs and stored on the soda dispenser grate. Store ice scoop properly at all times. Inspector suggests removing ice scoop overnight as ice can melt and scoop handle can fall into the ice.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

Take care to look at all utensils as they are being put away and remove utensils that are no longer smooth and easily cleanable. At least 5 spatulas were discarded during the inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Walls in the dish area have accumulated soil in areas around the caulk line of the 3 part sink and between the dirty dish collection area and the wall at the door. Clean and maintain free of accumulated soil.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment:
3-501.19: (A) If time without temperature used for public health control, written procedure approved by regulatory authority shall be available upon request (Pf). (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (P) (C) If time is used as control for up to 6 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F or less. FOOD shall not exceed 70F. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 6-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (D) HSP FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS cannot use time control for raw eggs. 
Observed the time tags on the salad bar read 2pm upon arrival. Inspector arrived at the facility at 2:40pm. Salad bar was the first area inspected. Food that did not look new was rotated out.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 
Observed several wet wiping cloth buckets to have wiping cloths hanging over the edges. Train employees to keep wiping cloths inside of the buckets when not in use.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.113: Observed old mop water and a mop sitting in the mop bucket. Ensure mops are hung so they can air dry and mop water is discarded after use. 
Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.
